messages:
Mira: Thinking out loud — we need a synthetic generator that stresses kernel selection + kv cache handoffs AND gives stable apples-to-apples numbers across quant/comp kernels. Current spike-only sims miss the long-tail KV churn we see in prod.

Toni: +1. What if we mix client zipf identities with layered QPS ramps so some clients ramp slow and some do sudden microbursts? That should exercise both batching heuristics and KV cache eviction patterns.

Ajay: Love the idea. Concrete sketch: a cascade of ramps where global QPS follows a slow sawtooth (mins) and superimposed on that are short 1–10s Poisson bursts for 10% of clients. That forces kernel handoffs when batch sizes spike.

Kai: For kernel selection profiling we need deterministic seeds so we can repro which kernel was chosen for a given seq_len/kv_state. Add per-trace metadata: seed, client_id, kv-hotset-id.

Luca: Also include a "cold-started KV" mode: periodically pause a subset of clients for 30–120s then resume to create cold KV cache misses. This will show the tail latency impact of KV warming and batching interplay.

Mira: Draft config (pseudo):
```json
{
  "global_pattern": "sawtooth(min=50,max=2500,period_mins=8)",
  "client_distribution": "zipf(s=1.1,clients=12000)",
  "microbursts": {"pct_clients": 0.12, "burst_dur_s": [1,10], "burst_qps_mul": [5,15]},
  "kv_working_set": {"per_client": 800, "hot_ratio": 0.18},
  "cold_cycles": {"pause_s": [30,120], "freq_per_hour": 2},
  "deterministic_seed": 123456
}
```

Toni: Nice. For apples-to-apples, we should run identical seeds across model variants and collect: p50/p95/p99 latencies, kernel-choice histogram, batch size distribution, kv-hit-rate over time, and token-cost.

Ajay: Can we also capture the "kernel switch events" timeline? E.g., whenever runtime switches to fallback kernel or quantized path, emit an event with context (seq_len, batch_size, kv_hot_fraction). That helps correlate regressions with traffic moments.

perf-bot: Experiment run queued: id=cascade-run-2026-03-18-01 seed=123456 variants=[fp16, int8-q4, int8-q2] expected_duration=2h. Will post summary when finished.

Kai: For batching heuristics experiment, add a toggle to let the generator emit short TTL-prefixed requests to exercise prefix cache reuse vs streaming new prefixes. Two modes: prefix-heavy vs prefix-diverse.

Luca: Observability checklist: trace IDs, request-level kernel hint, batch_id, kv_lookup_count, kv_cache_miss boolean. Export to s3 in newline-delimited JSON to ease offline correlation.

Mira: One more: add a "latency shaping" knob that injects tail-affecting client think-time distributions (weibull with heavy tail). That will push the end-to-end p99 especially when combined with cold KV events.

Toni: Sounds solid. Next steps: someone pair with infra to wire the deterministic seed into the harness, add the kernel switch event telemetry, then run 3 variants across 3 hardware families for apples-to-apples. I'll draft a checklist.

Ajay: I'll prototype the generator patch Monday. Will include a small CLI to produce a short local replay (10m) so devs can iterate without burning infra.

perf-bot: cascade-run-2026-03-18-01 completed: summary attached. fp16 p99=178ms, int8-q4 p99=192ms (+7.9%), int8-q2 p99=232ms (+30%). Kernel-switch spike correlation: 72% of p99 events overlap a kernel fallback within 300ms. KV-cold windows increased p99 by ~40% during warmup windows. Full logs: s3://redwood-perf/cascade/cascade-run-2026-03-18-01.jsonl

Mira: Thanks perf-bot — that delta is bigger than we hoped for int8-q2. We'll need to dig into which kernel path causes the extra latency. Ajay/Kai can you triage the switch traces from the q2 run?

Kai: On it. I noticed a pattern: when batch_size spikes above 18 with >30% kv-miss, we prefer the fallback kernel which has much worse startup cost. I'll open a short issue with trace snippets.

Luca: If fallback startup cost is the culprit, we can try: a) pre-warming fallback kernels during predicted microbursts, b) smoothing batch threshold to avoid sudden handoff, or c) micro-batching inside fallback to amortize startup. All have pros/cons.

Mira: Great discussion. Let's capture the generator config and the perf summary in a short runbook so PM/bench can reproduce. Also add a follow-up experiment that varies cold-cycle frequency.

Toni: I'll make the runbook and assign owners. Tagging @Ajay for prototype and @Kai for kernel-trace analysis. :thumbsup:
